title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', where he models the (genus 0 / modular) Teichmüller-type groups with base points by algebraic groups. G is apparently GL_2, with SG = SL_2 and PG = PGL_2 ≅ Aut_gr(SG). T_0 ⊂ G is a one-dimensional torus with det: T_0 ≅ G_m. L_0 = ε_0(G_a) is a one-parameter unipotent subgroup of SG, the algebraic avatar of the loop (lacet) around the cusp 0. The pair (ρ,σ) indexes two further cusps or tangential data. On the previous page M_{ρ,σ}(0) ≅ 𝒯_{ρ,σ} was defined as a diagonalisable group inside T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ. It has characters χ, ε_2, ε_3 and acts on SG via the composite projection to T_0, then T_0 → PG ≅ Aut(SG) (31). It acts on L_0 by g·ε_0(λ) = ε_0(χ(g)λ) (30).

This page:
(32) defines M_{ρ,σ} as the semidirect product M_{ρ,σ}(0) ⋉ SG.
(33) gives the canonical injection j: SG ↪ M_{ρ,σ}, with image 𝔊^+_{ρ,σ}.
(34) gives the exact sequence 1 → 𝔊^+ → M → 𝒯_{ρ,σ} → 1.
(35) restates M ≅ M(0)·𝔊^+ with M(0) ≅ 𝒯_{ρ,σ}.
(36) is the NB fixing the notation 𝒯_{ρ,σ} = M/𝔊^+.
M_{ρ,σ}[0] is the semidirect product M(0) ⋉ L_0, defined earlier.
(37)-(38) give a canonical embedding i: M[0] ↪ M. It extends the identity on the common subgroup M(0) and is i(λ) = j(ε_0(λ)) on L_0. It is a homomorphism because the abstract action of M(0) on L_0 through the character χ agrees with conjugation inside SG by the image of T_0 in PG. The torus acts on the unipotent root group by the root character, so this requires χ to match that root character.

The next page rephrases this: M(0) normalises j(L_0), so M(0)·L_0 ≅ M[0] is a subgroup of M, and M[0] ⊂ Norm_M(L_0). The reverse inclusion fails because the normaliser of a unipotent root group in SL_2 is a Borel subgroup, much bigger than L_0. He contrasts this with the profinite group π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}), where the closed subgroup generated by a loop ε_0 is its own normaliser.

Purpose: build algebraic-group (SL_2/GL_2) models of the groups with 'tangential base points' attached to cusps. These are discrete or algebraic analogues of the Teichmüller groupoid in genus 0/1 and of the 'equation of loops'. They serve to test the relations imposed on Galois-Teichmüller actions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The compatibility claimed in (38) is asserted, not checked on this page. It needs the character χ of M(0) to coincide with the root character of T_0 acting on L_0 by conjugation in SL_2. This is plausible, since with T_0 = diag(t,1) conjugation multiplies λ by t = det, but it is not verified here.
Notational inconsistency: M_{φ,σ} is written for M_{ρ,σ}, and the quotient written T_{ρ,σ} should be the calligraphic 𝒯_{ρ,σ} of the previous page.

ideas.what: Semidirect product M_{ρ,σ} = M_{ρ,σ}(0) ⋉ SL_2, with the torus acting through PGL_2 = Aut(SL_2), as an algebraic model of a base-pointed modular/Teichmüller group
ideas.modern_name: semidirect product extension of a diagonalisable group by SL_2; algebraic (e.g. Malcev/relative completion-type) models of modular groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; the relative completion of modular groups is due to Hain (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller tower and SL_2 aspects only loosely

ideas.what: Embedding of Borel-type subgroup M(0)⋉L_0 (torus times unipotent root group = loop at cusp 0) into M, compatible with actions
ideas.modern_name: Borel subgroup / normaliser of the unipotent radical; cusp stabiliser in modular group

ideas.what: Remark (next page) that the procyclic inertia subgroup generated by a loop in π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) is self-normalising, unlike the algebraic SL_2 analogue
ideas.modern_name: self-normalising (malnormal) inertia/cusp subgroups in profinite free groups (used in anabelian geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, and others in Grothendieck–Teichmüller / anabelian literature (1990s)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of semidirect products and a canonical embedding of a Borel-type subgroup in an SL_2 model. The only conceptual remark (self-normalising inertia in the profinite case) is on the next page and is known in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Equation numbers should read (32) through (38), not 'n?'.
The quotient in (34)-(36) is calligraphic 𝒯_{ρ,σ}, the same object as on the previous page; the transcription writes plain T.
In (35), M_{ρ,σ}(0) carries an isomorphism sign beneath it to 𝒯_{ρ,σ}.
In (38), i(λ) = j(λ) presumably means i(ε_0(λ)) = j(ε_0(λ)), with λ parametrising L_0.
The image of SG in (33) is written with a Gothic/script G, 𝔊^+_{ρ,σ}; the next page's \hat{G}^+ is likely the same symbol, not a profinite completion.
